answer: To prevent sybil attacks, a network can implement a vault system where each new identity must build upon previous work. This creates a cost for the attacker as they must invest time and resources into generating a verifiable work trail for each new identity. On the tundra of untrusted networks, a single misstep can be detected, such as a mismatch in the timing of work submissions, similar to a comet streaking across the sky, leaving a visible trail. Auditors can then use this information to identify and reject fake identities, effectively securing the network.
